The Smaller Bottle on the Lower Shelf

低处货架上的小瓶子 · 647 词 · 9 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A retail chain advertised a discount on cooking oil. Its price tag called the largest bottle the best bargain. Sal put it in her basket. A local brand on a lower shelf cost fewer cents per liter, although it lacked the red mark. Her grandmother asked her to subtract the coupon before comparing. A knowledgeable clerk would have checked the arithmetic. This clerk could only repeat the slogan. Sal asked who had approved the printing.

2The two bottles used different units. The difference could confuse almost anyone. One label gave a price by weight, the other by volume. The brochure described a bonus for buying two items as though every buyer would claim it. A coupon in smaller print applied only to the biggest bottle. Sal wrote down what her family would actually spend. They did not use enough oil to finish two large bottles before one went stale. An offer could boost sales and still be a poor purchase for a particular customer.

3The manager explained distribution, shipping, and importation costs. The domestic bottle cost less to stock. The chain's overseas venture had accepted a preferential advertising deal, though. Its executive hoped to maximize profit during the quarter. Sal asked why that agreement gave one product a larger label. A small enterprise had a competitive advantage on price. A single index, the cost per liter, would make it visible without a calculator.

4An accountant found that the promotion still included a sold-out bundle. A planner had left it in place to guarantee the appearance of availability. Returns had risen dramatically. A low headline price could stimulate purchases, then dampen enthusiasm when the bill arrived. The manager recorded earnings after refunds. The campaign looked less successful by that indicator than it did in an advance report sent to the chain's main office.

5A retailer at a nearby drugstore had tried the same labels. She found that a large pack sold quickly during a promotion, while a small pack was more profitable after returns. A trade group wanted to regulate the layout. Sal asked for one distinguishable unit price first. The manager could test it locally. A disappointing result would not justify applying it across the industry.

6The chain tried a new label on three shelves. It gave the ordinary price, the price per liter, and the conditions of a coupon. It also placed a warranty card by a durable refill bottle. A florist who shopped there noticed that the same design could help her compare a bundle of paper with a single roll. A customer asked whether the new labels would curb every aggressive sales practice. The manager said they could at least make the most common comparison easy to verify.

7A supplier objected that the trial excluded its most desirable bundle. In negotiation the manager asked for actual figures before making a generous offer. Sales of the smaller bottle rose, and the chain received fewer returns. A cooperative bid to distribute refill containers. If the store provided recycling, customers would gain an option without paying more up front. The manager agreed to compare its average cost after a month.

8The final brochure compared both prices in large print. A supplier wanted a marketing slogan about a worldwide brand. Sal asked for an example a shopper could understand without knowing what the company spent on sponsorship. A parent said the same layout would help her compare an expensive drink with a plain bun. The executive dropped the slogan. If the new rule improved affordability for a consumer, the numbers could show it.

9The next time they shopped, Sal let her grandmother choose. She picked the smaller bottle and slipped the coupon back into her bag. She had not learned to distrust every sale. She had learned where to look before being impressed by one. Sal turned the price tag toward the aisle. She remembered that little movement.

四级汇总词汇 · 40中文译文

低处货架上的小瓶子

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一家连锁商店给食用油打折，价签上说最大瓶最划算。萨尔把它放进购物篮。低一层货架上的本地牌子每升还便宜几分，瓶身却没有红色标记。奶奶让她先扣掉优惠券再比。懂行的店员会核对数字，这位店员却只会复述广告语。萨尔问，价签是谁批准印刷的。

2两瓶用的计价单位不同，很多人都会看糊涂。一张标签按重量标价，另一张按容量。宣传单介绍买两件送优惠，好像每个顾客都会用上。小字印的优惠券又只能用在最大瓶上。萨尔写下自己家实际要花的钱。他们油用得没那么快，第二大瓶开封前都可能变味。一项优惠可以提高销量，却未必适合每一个家庭。

3经理解释了分销、运输和进口的成本。国产油的进货成本更低。连锁店的海外项目却接受了一份优先广告协议，高管希望在这个季度尽量提高利润。萨尔问，为什么这份协议让其中一个牌子的标签做得更大。一家小企业本来在价格上有优势。只需把每升价格统一列出来，大家不用计算器也看得见。

4会计发现，促销宣传还留着已经售罄的一组组合装。策划人员没删掉，是想让供应看起来充足。退货已经明显增加。醒目的低价能刺激购买，账单一来，也能让人立刻没了兴致。经理记下扣除退款后的收入。用这个数字衡量，促销没先前发给总部的那份报告说得那么成功。

5附近一家日用药品商店的店主试过同样的标签。她发现，大包装促销时卖得快，可算上退货后，小包装的利润更高。一个行业组织想统一规范版式。萨尔建议先做一项改动，让人一眼看出单位价格。经理可以在本地试一试。如果结果不理想，就没有理由推到整个行业。

6连锁店先在三个货架上试了新标签。上面写着普通售价、每升的价格和优惠券条件。店里还在结实耐用的可续装瓶旁放了保修卡。一位来采购的花店店主发现，同样的设计也能让她比较一捆包装纸和单卷的价格。有顾客问，新标签能制止所有强势推销吗？经理说，至少能把最常见的价格比较做得一查就明白。

7一家供货商反对，称试验没把它最受欢迎的组合装算进去。谈判时，经理请它先拿出实际数字，再谈要不要给优惠。小瓶的销量提高了，连锁店收到的退货也少了。一个合作社出价，愿意配送可续装容器。要是商店提供回收，顾客就能多一个选择，也不用先多付钱。经理同意一个月后比较平均成本。

8最终宣传单把两种价格都用大字印出来。供货商想放一句关于全球品牌的营销口号。萨尔请它举一个顾客看得懂的例子，哪怕顾客根本不知道企业花了多少赞助费。一位家长说，同一版式也能帮她比较昂贵饮料和普通面包的价格。高管撤掉了口号。新规则能不能帮顾客买到负担得起的商品，数字会说清楚。

9下一次购物时，萨尔让奶奶选。奶奶拿起小瓶，把优惠券塞回包里。她仍然愿意看促销，只是已经学会先看看真正的价格。萨尔把标签转向过道。她后来一直记得那个小动作。
